Citation_Information.description: This multi-part table contains three sections. The first is a single line that includes the number of vertices and the number of facets that make up the shape model of Helene. The second contains position location for all of the vertices of the model. The third section defines the plates by referencing three vertices (from the second section) for each plate.

Table_Character.description: This is a single row of data that lists the number of vertices and facets that make up this shape model of Helene, derived solely from Cassini ISS Narrow Angle Camera data.

Field_Character.name: NUMBER_OF_VERTICES
Field_Character.description: Number of vertices that define the plates of the shape model.

Field_Character.name: NUMBER_OF_FACETS
Field_Character.description: Number of facets defining the triangular plates in the shape model.

Table_Character.description: Table of vertices of numerical shape model of Saturn's satellite Helene. These are the vertices of plates that approximate the surface of Helene. Each row of this table contains the X, Y and Z coordinates of one vertex in a Cartesian coordinate system that is fixed with respect to Helene's body-fixed rotating reference frame. The origin of the coordinate system is coincident with Helene's model center of figure to an accuracy of about 10 m. The +Z axis of the coordinate system is coincident with Helene's North spin pole. The +X axis of the coordinate system is coincident with Helene's Prime Meridian, which on average points toward Saturn. The coordinate system is right-handed, with the +Y being opposite to direction of Helene's orbital motion (trailing side).

Table of triangular plates of numerical shape model of Helene. These triangular plates approximate the surface of Helene. Each row of this table contains three integer offsets that point to three vertices from the previous table. Those three vertices are the vertices of one triangular plate of the shape model. Each integer is the offset from the first row in the table of vertices, thus THE COUNTING STARTS FROM ZERO. An offset of 0 points to the first row in the table of vertices, an offset of 1 to the second row, and so on.
